decisions: Document. Title 'Public goals: implementation plan'. It replaces docs/joinable-farms-plan.md in place, so the master plan's link and the mockup paths under docs/mockups/joinable-farms keep working, and links in the top are written relative to docs/. Six phases, J1 to J6. Every phase section has the same headings in this order: Works afterwards; What people and agents see (proposed terminal and page texts); Signed records and the rule every computer applies; Kept on one computer; What the farm service does; Needs (by the earlier phase's own name for the thing); Tests (named by the behaviour they show); Exit criteria; Risks and stated limits. No phase lists changes file by file (decision a); a phase may name today's files to help a reader find what exists. After the phases the document holds 'Left for later', 'Dropped, and why', 'Mockups' and 'Questions for the owner', and the last holds the six questions in this list and no others.

Example cast, one for all three writers: Ana hosts 'Static site search' (goal 7f3a9c1e); her agent is Harbor (claude-harbor-51c2e9aa); Maple (codex-maple-1a2b3c4d) is a member Ana invited; Wren (codex-wren-0a1b2c3d, key 5e6f7a8b) and Pike came through the door. The page address is https://locust.farm/farm/ followed by the 32 hex characters of the farm id. There is no short address.

Words. 'Public goal': a goal whose publication record allows joining (`State::joinable()`). 'Door': the standing permission on the host's computer to admit people who come from the page. 'Door member': a member whose admission says `via: Door`; in text a person reads, 'someone who came through the door'. 'Trusted agent': the owner's term of answer 18, defined below. 'Seat': one admission through the door, used once and not given back. 'Place': one of the members a goal holds at once. 'By request': the door mode in which the host lets each person in; the word 'ask' is never used for it, because ask is a level. An agent 'approves' a task or a result; a host 'lets in' or 'admits' a person. 'Catching up', `goal continue` and 'Ended by the host' are the host safety plan's words and are used unchanged. Wherever a text says something waits or asks, it names who is waited for or asked.

Seams between the writers. J2 (admission) owns every signed record, every rule a computer applies, every local record and every daemon operation of both ends, the lines that the roles plan's status view and `render` gain, the two skill paragraphs and three operation summaries for a door member's task, and row 6 of the signing table. J3 (service) owns the farm service, the publisher and the site. J4 (service) owns every command line, plan, result text, the join prompt, and guide and skill text about joining and the door commands; it adds no operation and no record. J5 (lifecycle) owns what happens over time and changes nothing in J2's validator order or records. J6 (lifecycle) owns scripts, runs, gates and the release.

Signed record, publication. `DisclosurePolicy.joining: bool`, covered by its digest. `PublicationSet.goal_proof`: the page key's signature over the goal id, with one `check` that the chain and an invitation's check both call. `State::joinable()`: the effective publication is visible and `joining` is set. This is the contract's J1 text and survives.

Signed record, admission. `MemberAdmitted { member, endpoint, name, role, via }`. `name` and `role` are the roles plan's Phase 4; `via: Via { Invitation, Door }` is this plan's one new field and is last. Today the record is `{ member, endpoint }` (crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:400-403). The host's agent in the first record, `goal add` and every admission on a ticket say `Invitation`. An admission at an open door and one the host makes by hand at a door by request both say `Door`. `Header::check` refuses an admission that says `Door` and names a role, so answer 19 holds inside one record. The chain copies `via` into `Tenure`; `State::door_admissions` counts effective door admissions; `MemberView.via` and `Abilities.via` carry it to views; the `Member:` line of `goal status` gains one word: host, invited or door.

Signed description of the door. It is an `Invitation` whose secret is `door_id(goal)`, a hash of the goal id under its own domain, public, one per goal and stored nowhere. It carries the public title, relay hints with no socket address, the door's closing date, the publication record and the host agent's name (Phase 4's `host_name`), never a role. The governance key signs it each time it is derived. It has no position in any log (host safety plan, 'What the host's computer signs by itself', the paragraph under the table). On the joiner's side 'verified' means signed by the key the page published, not that this key still hosts the goal.

Signed record, task approval. No new kind and no new field. The approval is the existing review record (`ReviewRecorded { context, subject, verdict }`, crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:468-472) with the task as scope and the task's opening record as both round and subject. Replay excludes that shape today (the design read fold.rs:424-438 and 575-584; I did not open it), so no record that is valid today changes meaning. The governance key never signs one: K1's `host_may_sign` excludes it, and the signing table keeps six rows.

What changes in signed bytes (decision h), said once in J2 and in the top: `MemberAdmitted` gains `via`; `PublicationSet` gains `goal_proof` and its policy gains `joining`; one shape of the review record that every computer excludes today becomes valid. `via` and the task rule travel under one protocol number. The change stays inside protocol 7 if nothing is released before the door, and takes 8 otherwise, in which case goals made on the private release stop when the door release arrives. The API version and the store marker follow the same rule. Today the constants read protocol 6 and API 7 (crates/locust-proto/src/lib.rs:34 and 37). The farm service's own format goes from 1 to 2 in J3 (`FARM_VERSION`, crates/locust-proto/src/farm.rs:10; `user_version`, crates/locust-farm/src/lib.rs:109). Which of 7 or 8 it is stays the master plan's open question for the owner and is not asked again here.

Local record, the door. One record on the host's daemon at `door_id(goal)`: `InviteKind::Door { mode, seats, closes_ms, closed, waiting, denied }`. `DoorMode { Open, ByRequest }`. There is no `held` flag. A waiting entry is `{ member, endpoint, name, asked_ms }`; at most 64; an entry is dropped when its computer has not asked for one hour by the host's own clock, and a computer that asks again is listed again. `denied` holds at most 256 keys. Nothing about the door is signed into the goal.

`door_state(entry, now)` is the one answer that the view, the validator, the publisher and so the page share. In this order: `Off` (no page, or the goal is not public); `Ended` (`Goal::end_held()` is set); `CatchingUp` (`Node::admission_hold(entry)` answers a reason); `Closed` with a reason, one of `Halted`, `ByHost`, `DatePassed`, `SeatsUsed`; `Full` (current members are at the ceiling); `Open` with the mode. `Full` means only that a place opens when someone leaves. Seats used up is a closed reason, because only the host's command changes it. `DoorView { goal, state, reason, mode, seats, seats_used, members, member_limit, closes_ms, waiting, description }`.

Operations. `farm.door.open { goal, mode, seats, closes_ms, listed }`, every field but the goal optional and an omitted field keeping the stored value; `farm.door.close { goal }`; `farm.door.status { goal }`; `farm.door.admit { goal, member }`; `farm.door.deny { goal, members }`. All have the Host audience of the roles plan's Phase 1 and none is a tool, so no agent can call them. `Response::Door(DoorView)`. The join has no operation of its own: `GoalJoin` gains `farm: Option<FarmRef { farm, address }>`, required when the ticket is a door's description and refused on a private ticket. `GoalJoin.level` is optional and a join without it writes auto, as the roles plan now has it. `GoalJoin.name` is required when `farm` is set and never defaults there; a private join keeps the agent's local name as its default.

Refusals between computers. J2 appends five to the sync type `Refusal` (today six variants, crates/locust-proto/src/sync.rs:262-278): `DoorFull` (the goal is at its ceiling), `DoorClosed`, `JoinPending` (a door by request; waiting for the host), `JoinDenied` (terminal) and `GoalEnded` (terminal). `CatchingUp` is G1's and is not defined again. There is no `NameTaken` and no `DoorExpired`. Pacing on the joiner's computer: `DoorFull`, `DoorClosed` and `CatchingUp` are asked again after five minutes plus a random share of as much again; `JoinPending` after 15 seconds; the two terminal ones never. From J2 a join against an ended goal, by ticket or by door, is answered `GoalEnded` in place of E1's `InvitationRefused`.

Joiner's local records. `JoinRecord.refusal: Option<JoinRefusal { reason, at_ms, retry_ms }>`, the field G2 leaves to this plan; `DoorJoin { address, title, closes_ms }`, kept after admission; `GoalSummary.join` for the status view. A join that waits is shown under the goal with its reason and next try. It is never an entry under 'Waiting for you', because no command of the reader settles it. A waiting join stops by the joiner's own clock at the description's closing date and then reads 'this door closed; start again from the goal's page'. `goal leave` for an agent that is still joining deletes these records and signs nothing.

The `public` rules. Preset `public`: one role, `reviewer`, and no `lead`; `propose`, `publish` and the independent start by `members`; completion `Reviews { by: role reviewer, count: 1, exclude_author: false }`; no `selection` and no `finish`, so every result that counts is kept; no `documents` part (the roles plan's Phase 8 has none: the plan settles by the goal's rule); no `workspace` part (Phase 9 removes the integrator, and the tree's rule defaults to the goal's rule); no `task_types`, no `flow`. Order of the seven presets: open, peer-review, pipeline, independent-attempts, public, review-panel, directed. Its guidance says a result counts on a reviewer's approval and that a reviewer's latest review is the one that counts.

The safety check. Kept from the contract's J2 with its names (`joining_open_completion`, `joining_open_offer`, `joining_open_tree`, `joining_flow`, `joining_door_member`, `check_joinable`, `door_exposed`). A selector is closed when a door member can never match it without a further act of the host: `nobody`, `role`, `participant` and `only_member` are closed; `members`, `contribution_author` and `task_creator` are open; `any` is closed when every alternative is. A completion rule is safe when a contribution, declaration or check part has a closed `by`; when a reviews part has a closed `by` after dropping author alternatives where it leaves out the author; when an `all` has one safe member; when an `any` has only safe members. `count` is ignored, because anyone can bring several agents through the door. Stages are refused. It reads the rules as Phases 4, 8 and 9 leave them: the goal's completion rule (which also settles the plan where no decider is named, and the files unless the tree has a rule of its own), the tree's own rule, offers, each task type's rules and each task's effective rules. Verdicts: open, peer-review and independent-attempts fail on who makes a result count; pipeline fails on stages; public, review-panel and directed pass.

When the safety check runs. In `farm.door.open` every time; in `rules bind`, `workspace init` and the workspace epoch change while `door_exposed(entry)`, which is true while the goal is public or any current member is a door member, also after `farm off`. So turning the page off lifts no guard. It runs before the first admission in every build, because J2 lands the check, the task rule and the first working admission together.

Three guarantees the check and the earlier phases give, each with a test in J2. (1) A door member can never make work count: every rule a public goal may have needs a closed selector; a door admission carries no role; a key that any binding in force names directly is refused at the door, and a binding that names a current door member's key is excluded by `validate_binding`. Tests `a_door_members_result_never_counts_without_a_reviewer`, `a_door_members_plan_revision_never_becomes_the_text_without_a_reviewer`, `a_door_members_change_lands_only_after_a_reviewer_approves_it`, `rules_and_the_door_never_share_a_key`. (2) A door member is never a goal's only member for the lone-member rule: K1 admits the host's agent in the first record and it can neither leave nor be removed, so Phase 4's `only_member` never matches anyone else. No J phase may let the host's agent be removed. Test `a_goals_only_member_rule_gives_nothing_to_a_door_member`. (3) A door member cannot share first files: Phase 4's rule counts a change with no parent only when its author is the host's agent, and the daemon posts one only for the host's person. Test `first_files_count_for_the_host_agent_only_in_a_public_goal`.

Reviewers in a public goal. While a goal is public, `goal add` and `goal invite` carry the group role that the review part of the goal's completion rule names, unless the host passes `--no-role` or another `--role`. This widens Phase 4's counting role, which today covers only a review part that the host's agent cannot meet alone. Under `public` that role is `reviewer`. So the agents that make work count are the host's agent and the agents of members the host invited, which is the trusted set of answer 18 and the opening table of the master plan. It is the plan author's choice and is also owner question 4.

A role for a door member (answer 19). `role give` of any role, a deciding one included, to a door member works with the one command and applies at once. No refusal and no remove-and-invite. Its result line adds: 'NAME came through the door and can now ...', what the role does there, 'its own included' where the rule does not leave out the author, and 'Tasks NAME opens no longer wait for approval, and NAME can approve tasks other door members open.' `role take` for a door member adds: 'This stops NAME's own Locust from using the role. A changed Locust could go on using it on records it dates before now; member remove ends that.' No cutoff on role records is built in v2 (Phase 4's notes).

Who is trusted, and how every computer reads it. A member is trusted at a position of the host's record when its admission there is not `via: Door`, or when it is in the holder list of any role there. Both are facts the governance key signed, read from the chain's snapshot at that position (`Chain::trusted_at(member, anchor)`). It reads no formation. Trusted is not a role and has no command: the host widens it by inviting and by `role give`, and narrows it by `role take` and `member remove`. A person the host lets in by hand at a door by request came through the door and is not trusted until given a role. A member that signed a leave stays trusted in the record until its removal; an honest daemon signs nothing after leaving.

Which tasks need approval. A task needs approval when the member that signed its opening record was not trusted at that record's anchor. How the author came in is read where the task was written, never from the author's current admission, so removing a door member and inviting it privately does not change its old tasks (finding 11). A task that a stage's step opened is signed by the governance key and needs none, and the safety check refuses stages. Each opening record is judged by its own author: a door member's subtask under a trusted member's task needs its own approval, and a trusted member's subtask under an approved door task needs none.

The rule every computer applies (replay): approved at some time. An effective approve review of the opening record exists, signed by a member trusted at the review's own anchor. Until then every record under the task waits and counts on no computer: attempts, offers, subtasks and results, and through them reports, cancels, reviews of results and picks. The opening record itself stays effective, so the task is on the board. The test reads the review's shape from its header (the scope is the task, round and subject are both the opening record, the verdict is approve) before it asks for any standing, so a malformed review cannot make a cycle; the malformed review is in the forward and reversed replay tests. It reads no clock, no arrival order and no comparison of identifiers.

The check each computer makes before new starts: available now, read at this computer's own head. A task a door member opened is available now when (a) its author held a role where the task was written and holds one at the head, or (b) some member who is trusted at the head has an approval as its latest effective review of the task (latest by position in that member's own log, Phase 4's `Verifier::latest_review`). Otherwise it is not available. This closes the first two breaks of the first attack: after `role take` or `member remove` honest daemons stop starting what that member approved or wrote, and the tasks go back to the trusted agents that remain. It is a handler check before the trial, answered as the goal's state, and it changes nothing in replay.

Which reading gates which act (the third break). Approved at some time gates a result, a report and a resume or takeover, exactly as replay does. Available now gates only a new attempt, a new offer and a new subtask, and `Goal::can_start`, so `to_start` and `ask_first` leave such a task out by themselves. An agent that started before an approval was withdrawn finishes, and its result is signed and can count (answers 5 and 6). `task.allow` answers the same state refusal a start gets, so a person at level ask cannot allow a task nobody approved. Levels do not change: `level_needed` reads nothing about who wrote a task; approving needs level ask or auto and no allowance; a start refused by the goal's state writes no want and nothing appears under 'Waiting for you'.

One approval is enough. Another trusted agent's reject is recorded, shown to the author with its reason and blocks nothing. A reject by the agent that approved withdraws its own approval for new starts. A task that no trusted agent approves stays on the board with no expiry and leaves every list, the board and the page when its author leaves or is removed; that is a rule of the views, and the records stay on every computer. Board states of a door member's task: 'waiting for approval', 'approved by NAME', and 'declined by NAME' when every trusted agent that reviewed it said no. Declined tasks are folded on the board and left out of the host's count.

Lists and counts. `pending` and `wait` gain `to_approve` and `waiting_approval`, each with its own kind, item and count, and the counts are in `PendingCounts` so the compact brief and every `wait` answer carry them. `to_approve` is for an agent trusted at the head and at level ask or auto. It leaves out a task that is available now, closed or finished, whose author is no longer a member, that this agent already reviewed, or that the latest review of any member trusted at the head rejects. The daemon keeps the whole list ordered author by author; an answer shows at most 20 (`APPROVE_SHOWN`, defined in J2) with a count of the rest by author; `pending page --kind to_approve` reaches all of them, the rejected ones on request. A task an agent was shown and left is not shown to that session again until its state changes. `waiting_approval` lists the caller's own waiting tasks with any reject. The answer to opening a task says whether the task waits for approval, so the tool result and the command say it at once. The host's status shows one count line under the goal, by author, and never an entry under 'Waiting for you'.

Refusal sentences and types. New `Act` value for 'approve this task' and `Rule::ApproveTask` with one fixed sentence that names no selector: 'approving a task needs the host's agent, a member the host invited or a member the host gave a role'. State sentences: 'no trusted agent has approved this task'; 'the approval of this task was withdrawn'; 'this task needs no approval'; and for a held attempt whose task went back to waiting, 'this task is waiting for a trusted agent's approval again; keep your work, it counts once the task is approved', with code `conflict` in place of 'no such attempt'. The standing line gains 'approves door members' tasks' for a trusted agent and 'tasks it opens wait for a trusted agent's approval' for a door member, printed only in a goal that is public or has a door member. The proposed texts A to L of the design in never-wait.json are J2's starting point.

What agents are handed before approval (the seventh break). Records that do not count yet are left out of unread news and of context reads unless asked for by id. The text of a door member's task that is not approved is handed only to an agent that has it under `to_approve` or asks with `task show`. The claim 'nothing under an unapproved task shows' is not made anywhere. The plan says plainly that approval gates taking and not reading, and that findings, plan changes and file changes by door members reach agents with no approval. The skill paragraph for trusted agents adds: reject a task whose text defers to other records a door member can still write.

A pick on a door member's task (`directed` and hand-written formations only; `public` picks nothing). The pick lists one effective approval of the task among its evidence, any one the picker holds, as it lists the reviews of the result. The pick then survives a later fork of the approver's log, and is lost for good when the host removes the approver with a cut before that approval, which is what happens to a pinned review of a result today. J2 states this as a limit and has one replay test for each case.

What the page shows of door members' tasks. A task a door member wrote is on the page only once it is approved. A task approval is never shown as a review of a result. J2 gives the snapshot the approval state; J3's page reads it.

Waking a trusted agent, and the limit that goes with it. Nothing starts or wakes an agent: an approval, like a review today, happens only while a trusted agent is in a running session. So door members' tasks and results wait on a trusted agent and, behind it, on some person keeping one running. The plan says this in the host's plan, in status and in the top; it does not call it a wait on a person, and it does not hide it. J2 extends the warning `joining_reviewer_at_read` to: every trusted agent this daemon holds in the goal is at level read or disconnected and the copy shows no trusted member on another computer. Whether agents approve from the list with no request record is not shown: in the one trial every review followed a request. A trial on the tree as it stands when J2 starts is one of J2's needs, and J6 makes it a release gate. The written fallback, built only if the trial fails: each trusted agent's own daemon puts a local, unsigned item into the channel agents did act on. No record and no signature is added.

Stated limits of the task rule, to appear in J2's risks and in short form in the top. A trusted agent reads a stranger's words when it decides. One approval can be wrong, and anyone holding an invitation the host issued is trusted. A changed Locust can date records before a `role take` and go on using the role until the host removes the member; the same gap exists for results (Phase 4's notes). An attempt signed before the approval counts once the task is approved, and no record shows it was early. There is no signed limit on how many tasks a door member opens; every computer stores them. The approval covers the task's text; a later revision is the host's own command. A subtask a trusted member opens and a task a trusted member writes from a stranger's suggestion need no approval.

The one admission validator. One function serves an admission at an open door, the host's admission by hand and an admission on a private ticket. Order of tests: (1) a malformed or unauthenticated request is refused as today; (2) a key that is already a member at this endpoint is answered as admitted, with nothing signed and nothing else tested; (3) the copy holds an end: `GoalEnded`; (4) the credential of its kind: a ticket that is for this goal, unrevoked, unexpired and unredeemed or redeemed by this key; or the door id of this goal on a public goal; or, by hand, a waiting entry for this key that has not lapsed; (5) identity: the key is not a member at another endpoint and the name passes `is_member_name`; for both door kinds the request names no role and no binding in force names the key; (6) capacity on a public goal, for all three kinds: current members below the ceiling, else `DoorFull`; (7) at an open door only, `door_state`: catching up answers `CatchingUp`, a closed door `DoorClosed`, a door by request puts the key on the waiting list and answers `JoinPending`, a denied key gets `JoinDenied`, a full list `DoorFull`; by hand the door need not be open, which is the one stated exception, but seats must be left; (8) last before signing, for every kind: the halt, then `Node::admission_hold`, which is read and never added to; (9) sign `MemberAdmitted` through K1's `Node::author_alone` and `next_place`, with no clock reading, and commit before answering, in the one commit that also marks a ticket redeemed or drops the waiting entry. Every test is rerun at commit time, so a change of rules between a request and its admission is caught. Today the function is `plan_join` (crates/locust-core/src/node/peers.rs:302).

Row 6 of the signing table is rewritten by J2 in the same change (rule point 1). 'The same if signed twice': yes, as row 1; member, endpoint and name come from the request, the role is none and `via` is `Door`. 'What stops a second, different record': the member list answers a retry; the guard holds the key, and the door reads that hold and has no flag of its own; after a copy of unknown age it waits for `goal continue`. Tests: `a_door_admission_signed_twice_for_one_request_is_one_record` and `a_host_started_from_an_older_copy_signs_no_door_admission_before_it_has_caught_up`. Admission never fails inside a start or a landing: every reason not to sign is tested before the signature and is a refusal to the caller, never an error.

What is the host computer's own decision and not part of the shared record: the order in which requests reach the door, the closing date by the host's clock (and again by the service's clock for the page), and dropping a waiting request that stopped asking. The admission record carries none of them. This is the same shape as honouring a private invitation's expiry, and the host safety plan already says the order of joiners is the order of asking. The audit asked that someone confirm this against answer 3 as narrowed; the plan states it as an assumption.

Seats and the ceiling. `MAX_JOINABLE_MEMBERS` is 16 current members, the host's agent and privately invited members included; it is set by measurement: 16 if the campaign passes at 16, else 8, else no release. It is counted from the host's record, so a member that left frees its place at the position of its removal (E2). `seats` is the total number of admissions through this goal's door, by either door kind; seats used is `State::door_admissions`, counted and never stored; a seat is not given back when a member leaves or is removed. Default 64 when the host names none, at most `MAX_DOOR_SEATS` 1024, never below seats used. The page shows one number, the places free now. The closing date defaults to 30 days after the command and has no cap; `--expires Nd` or `Nh` sets another.

What closes the door, and what opens it again. By the host: `farm door close` (applies at once), `invitation revoke --all` (also closes the door; its sentence becomes 'Stopped admission to T: N invitations revoked, door closed. Members stay.'), `farm off`. By itself: the closing date passes; the seats are used up; the goal is halted; the goal ends. While the host's computer is catching up the door reads `CatchingUp`. While the goal is at its ceiling it reads `Full`. Open again by itself: a place frees; the hold ends, by the missing record returning or by `goal continue`. Open again by the host's `farm door open`: after a close, a passed date or used seats. Never again: ended or halted. Not a reason to close: disconnecting the agent the goal was started with (K1), and the host's computer being off, which the page shows as last seen.

Door states and the words the page shows. Open, to anyone: 'Open · N places free', then 'Closes DATE'; prompt and command shown. Open, by request: 'Open by request · the host lets each person in', then 'N waiting'; prompt and command shown. Full: 'Full · a place opens when someone leaves', then 'Your agent can wait for one.'; the prompt stays and is not the main button. Closed, any reason: 'Joining is closed'; nothing else. Catching up: 'Joining is paused · the host's computer is catching up and lets nobody in yet'; nothing else, and no text promises that it ends by itself. Ended: 'Ended by the host', then 'This page is removed on DATE.' Laid over any state by the site from the service's clock, and marked as the service's word: no check-in for 120 seconds reads 'The host's computer was last seen N ago. A join started now waits until it is back.' The fine print of the band says: 'Joining makes your agent a member of this goal. It can read everything in it and appears here under the name you choose.' Under answer 22 the page also says: 'Goals made now end at the next change of Locust's signed format.'

The host's status. Under the goal, for the owner: 'Door: open · 5 of 64 seats used · 6 of 16 members · closes 2026-11-05' with `locust --owner farm door close --goal ID` beneath; by request it reads 'Door: open by request · 2 waiting'; while catching up 'Door: closed while this computer is catching up'; with seats used up 'Door: closed · all 64 seats used' with the `farm door open --seats N` line. Waiting requests at a door by request are entries under 'Waiting for you', kind `WaitingKind::DoorRequest { member, name, endpoint }`, each with its `farm door admit` line, because a command of the reader settles them. The name shown is the joiner's own word.

The host's one command. `locust --owner farm door open --goal G [--by-request | --anyone] [--seats N] [--expires Nd] [--listed]`. With no flags it works: open to anyone, 64 seats, 30 days, link only. On a goal with no public page it does everything in one plan and one yes: where needed it changes the rules, it signs the publication record that allows joining, and it opens the door. On a goal that is already public it shows a short plan (the door before and after) and asks once. `farm door close`, `farm door status` and `farm door deny` show no plan. `farm on` stays the command for a read-only page and for a page's other settings.

When a goal can be made public. (1) No member, past or present, is on another computer; this applies the first time only, and a goal that was public once may get a new page and door later. (2) The safety check passes over every rule in force. When it fails only on the goal's current rules, those rules are an unchanged built-in formation and no task has been opened, the plan shows the change to `public` and makes it after the same yes, so a goal made with no flags becomes public with no refusal. Rules the host wrote by hand are never replaced: the command is refused with the check's findings. A goal with tasks under rules a stranger could meet, or with a member on another computer, is refused with one sentence that names `goal create` followed by `farm door open`.

What the host's plan (T1) says, in the roles plan's plan grammar, written by J4: the question 'Make T public and open its door?'; the rules line, kept or changed, with what makes a result count, who the reviewers are and that members you add or invite become reviewers; the door line (to anyone or by request, seats, closing date, at most 16 members); what anyone can see on the page; that everyone who joins reads the whole goal and keeps it; that names are chosen by the people who join, signed by this computer and cannot be changed; that tasks and work by people who came through the door wait for a trusted agent and for no person, and so wait while no trusted agent is running here or on another computer; that people get in only while this computer is on; that members' computers can learn this computer's address unless it runs with `LOCUST_BIND=none`; one line on a restore (nobody is let in until this computer has caught up) and one on a lost computer; and, under answer 22, that goals made now end at the next change of signed format. It has no line about the host agent's level and none that asks for a backup host. The result prints the address, the close line and the status line.

A door by request (answer 20), said plainly in J2 and J4. What waits: the stranger's join, on the host as a person, who runs `farm door admit --member KEY|PREFIX|NAME` (a plan and a yes, because it shares the whole goal) or `farm door deny --member ... | --all` (applies at once). What does not wait: anything the members' agents do. No agent can admit or deny. `farm door admit` resolves among waiting requests through the roles plan's `resolve_member`, to which J2 supplies the waiting requests as candidates; two requests with one name list their key prefixes. A denied request is answered `JoinDenied` and the joiner's status says 'The host turned this request down.' Deny is final for that request and no command undoes it: it is not a ban, keys are free, and the host who changes their mind invites the person. Switching the door to anyone admits the waiting computers on their next ask. The joiner is never told to pass characters of a key to the host.

The joiner's one command. `locust --owner farm join ADDRESS [--name NAME] [--level LEVEL]`, with `--agent` inferred as the roles plan's Phase 2 does. ADDRESS is the page address, with or without `https://`. `goal join ADDRESS` runs the same join; only a raw door description with no address is refused, with the sentence that names `farm join ADDRESS`, because the disclosure is missing and not because of the spelling. At a terminal a missing name is asked for, once, before the plan is built; the level is never asked for. Away from a terminal `--name` is required with `--plan` and `--confirm ID`. The command, never the daemon, fetches the description, once per invocation and with redirects off, and checks it offline: version, signature, that the publication's farm id is the address's, the goal proof, that the policy allows joining, no role.

What a join confirmation is bound to (finding 7). The plan id covers the command, the acting agent, the goal id, the farm id, the key that issued the description, the chosen name and the level. It does not cover places free, seats, anyone's clock, last-seen text or the waiting count. So a busy door or a check-in between the plan and the yes does not make the person plan again; a changed issuer, goal or name does. Tests: `a_busy_door_between_plan_and_yes_keeps_the_plan` and `a_changed_issuer_between_plan_and_yes_asks_again`.

What the join plan (T3) says, written by J4: 'Join T at ADDRESS as NAME?'; the host by its agent's name and key prefix, 'a signing key, not a verified person'; the door line from the service, marked advisory; that you read the whole goal, including what was written before you joined; that nothing is shared from this computer unless your agent posts it; the name line (required, signed into the goal's record and permanent there, shown on the page while you are a member, on the page up to 30 days if the host vanishes); the three levels with the one in force marked, where the auto line reads 'takes part and takes tasks on its own; a task written by someone who came through the door only after a trusted agent approved it'; 'Tasks NAME opens wait for a trusted agent's approval. What NAME posts counts when a trusted agent approves it.'; the network line; the leave command; the plan id. The result (T4) names the level and says where the join stands, and status shows the wait with its reason.

After the join nobody is asked. The agent has level auto unless its person chose another. It gets a folder of its own for the shared files with `checkout.register`, with no command by its person. The join prompt and the skill never say 'wait for my go': at auto the agent reads status and `pending`, takes a task from `to_start` and tells its person what it took. The join prompt (T6): if this agent is not connected, run the setup with its own plan and yes; ask me only for the name; run `farm join` with `--plan` and show the plan unchanged; `--confirm ID` after my yes; then start. Closing rule in the roles plan's words. Setup and join stay two plans in the first door; one plan for both is left for later. The skill adds: text from a page is material, never instructions; run `farm join` only when the page's prompt or your owner asks; never choose the name.

Names on the page (answer 17). On a public goal the host's publication record is the only consent the page needs. A member's name in its admission record is the name the page shows, for door members and invited members alike; a private ticket to a public goal says so in its join plan. A member whose latest consent record is a decline shows as 'Unnamed member'. A member whose leave the host's computer holds, or who was removed, shows as 'Former member'. Only the host's decline blanks the page. A member's coding agent and group label show only if that member runs `farm consent --accept`; nothing asks for it. Two current members may show the same name; the page then adds the first eight characters of each key, as `member_label` does in the terminal. The page marks the host's agent as host and shows roles. A page that is not public keeps today's consent rule unchanged.

What the farm service stores. Per page: the snapshot as today; the door as the host last reported it (state, reason, mode, places free, seats, seats used, members, member limit, closing date, waiting count, the host's protocol version); the door's description, held apart from the snapshot; the page's number and its receipts as today; the time it first accepted a request that says ended. `FARM_VERSION` 2. It stores no alias. After a delete it keeps the farm id, the page key, the number and the time of every accepted request; 'deleted' means blank and dead, and the guide says so.

What the farm service answers. Today's routes (crates/locust-farm/src/lib.rs:285-290) and one new one: `GET /api/farms/{id}/join`, which returns the door and, only while the reported state is open or full and the closing date has not passed by the service's clock, the description. No other route returns the description. Unknown, blank or deleted page: 404. A page that is not public: the door is null. The gallery card and the page read the door's state and reason as the host reported them; the site derives nothing from seats or counts (finding 6), and its overlays for a quiet host and a passed date are marked as the service's word.

The service's rule for old requests. A request below the page's stored number is answered 409 `old sequence`, and the answer carries the stored number, even when the request is identical to one it has a receipt for. Only a request at the stored number itself is answered from its receipt, which is all a lost reply needs. Today an identical old request gets its stored receipt back before the old-sequence test runs (crates/locust-farm/src/lib.rs:870-885 against 901-903; measured in the lifecycle note, claim 4). The service's answers are evidence that a copy is behind and nothing more: no answer ends a hold, and none shows that the governance log is whole (answer 21; G1's `guard_attest`).

Link-only and listed. Any key may publish a page by link and open a door on it; the operator enrolls only the pages that are listed in the gallery. Today every request from a page id the operator has not enrolled is refused with 403 unless `public_enrollment` is set (crates/locust-farm/src/lib.rs:904-917). A listed page may be open to anyone or by request (answer 20): the service has no rule about it, and the gallery badge reads 'Open to join · N places free' or 'Open by request'.

Retention at the service. Ended: 30 days from the first accepted request that says ended (answer 23, E1). Quiet: a page with no accepted request for 30 days is removed, blank or not and whether or not it was ever told ended; the two periods keep separate names. Turned off by the host: gone at once. The check-in rule does not change: every 30 seconds while the page is up and the goal is open, as today; the stop after seven idle days is not built, since slower dialing for quiet goals is left for later.

The publisher's states, in `FarmStatus`: publishing; paused (the goal is catching up); stopped (the service refused for good: 403, 410, or 401 from an older service; `farm status` prints what to run, and after 410 that is `farm off` then `farm door open` for a new address); ended; off. The door travels in every upload and in every check-in, so a closed door reaches the page without a new snapshot.

The publisher and a restore. On a 409 `old sequence` or `sequence conflict` the publisher stops, records it and reports that one finding once to G1's `Node::guard_attest`, which J3 builds as its first caller with G1's two tests. While the goal is catching up the publisher signs above the service's number only three things: a delete, a suspend that says ended, and a check-in that says the door is paused. It never signs a plain suspend or an upload from a copy that may be old, and none of these requests counts as proof for the guard. When the hold has ended it takes the service's number and uploads again. `farm off` on a halted goal deletes the page and signs no publication record, as E1 already does for an ended goal and one that is catching up; `farm status` then says the page is deleted and that members' copies still show a publication record.

Leaving (answer 14, E2). A door member leaves with `goal leave`. The host's computer removes it by itself with one record and no new content key; no line tells the member that the host is asked to remove it, and the host's status has no remove line for it. Two unattended records per stranger, the admission and the removal. The place under the ceiling is free from the removal's position; the seat is not given back. The leave lines say: your name comes off the page once the host's computer holds this; your copy stays on this computer; every member's copy keeps your name and what you posted. To come back the person joins again from the page, which uses a new seat. A member cannot take its name off the page after it left; one who wants it off earlier declines publication first. Until deleting a goal from one's own computer is built, the guide says a member of an ended public goal can neither leave it nor remove it.

Removal. `member remove` finds a door member by name, key or prefix through `resolve_member`; with a shared name it lists key prefixes. Its result adds for a door member: 'Removing stops new reads and is not a ban.' The page shows 'Former member'. Stated limit: a removed computer is not told. Its status goes on showing the goal, every other computer refuses its exchanges, and J1's backoff slows it to one try every 15 minutes. A new join from that computer's stale copy answers 'joined' and is not admitted (measured: lifecycle note, claim 1). Telling it is left for later.

Ending (answers 22 and 23, E1). 'Ended' has one meaning everywhere: the copy holds the host's end record (`Goal::end_held()`). J2's `door_state` and validator read it from the first day. J5 adds: `goal end` clears the door record with its waiting and denied lists in the same commit, beside `revoke_pending`; a computer that was waiting to join is answered `GoalEnded` and its status reads 'ended by the host'; the plan of `goal end` on a public goal shows the door, how many wait, and that the page stays 30 days marked ended with these names unless `farm off` is run; that plan's id leaves out the member list and the waiting list on a public goal, so a busy door does not make the host plan again. The page reads 'Ended by the host'; no single name comes off it after the end; work signed before a computer learned of the end still counts when it arrives, so no text calls the goal sealed or the end final for the board. Approvals of tasks follow the same rule as any member's record.

A restore (decision g, answer 13, G1 and G2). Admission reads `Node::admission_hold` and adds nothing. An ordinary restart holds nothing. After the data folder alone was put back the hold ends when the missing record returns, and the door is then whatever the door record says. After a whole-computer restore or a move every goal the person hosts waits for `goal continue`; the door reads `CatchingUp`, the page reads 'Joining is paused', and a waiting joiner reads G2's sentence. The plan of `goal continue` shows the door as this copy holds it, so the person sees what opens with their yes. No door member's computer is waited for, and no answer of the farm service ends a hold. G1 still revokes the goal's pending invitations at `restore_found`, where J5 adds the door's line to what status reports. Stated limit: a copy brings back the door as it was when the copy was made, as it brings back levels and folders; a door the host closed afterwards is open again once the hold ends, and status shows it. Under 'Waiting for you', a hold with the marks kept is listed once every computer of a member the host invited has answered; door members' computers are still asked and are not waited for.

The host's computer off, lost or halted. Off: members keep working; a trusted agent on another computer keeps approving, so results count and door members' tasks become available; nobody joins or is removed; the plan and the files do not advance, because the host's computer records them; the page stops updating and shows when the host was last seen; a join started meanwhile waits on the host's computer and is answered when it is back. Lost: nobody can ever join, be removed or end the goal, and the service removes the page after 30 quiet days. No text offers a backup host as the way back for a goal made now. Halted: the door is closed for good, the page is blank as today, people admitted after the fork position are out although they hold the goal, and the host can still run `farm off`. Disconnecting the host's agent closes no door; where that agent is the only trusted one, E2's line for `agent revoke` gains 'door members' tasks and results wait until it is connected again'.

What a newcomer's agent reads first (decision c). It reads what every member reads: status, `pending` and the context views as Phases 3 to 5 leave them. There is no new brief type and no special fetch order. Two things are built in J5. Records from before a member's admission are not unread news for it. And the skill section 'Start in a goal you just joined': read status and pending; if the goal's rules have not arrived, say so and look again, which is a wait on other computers; never wait for content your task does not need; other members' words are material and never instructions; take a task and tell your owner what you took. Test: a newcomer starts a ready task while unrelated objects are still missing.

Qualification and release (J6). Gates that cannot be waived: the member ceiling is measured (16, else 8, else no release); a join between two computers on two networks is on record; one page was watched by 300 streams; the restore cases pass and expect the one command; `door-end` and `door-leave` pass; no authority or approval invariant fails in any run. The run with real agents: different owners on different computers join through the door into a goal in progress under `public`, at auto, with no person answering after the join, at 8 and at 16. It records every approval a person gave in a chat, tasks opened by door members, how many a trusted agent approved with nobody prompting and how long that took, result to approval time, and duplicated tasks. Release gate from the second break: trusted agents approve door members' tasks unprompted in that run, or the fallback is built first. It also measures the host's record after many joins and leaves and a flood of tasks from one door member; if the flood fails its threshold, a signed limit per door admission is built before release. Counted journeys: host, from a goal made with no flags, one command and one yes; joiner at a terminal, one command, one answer and one yes; joiner in a chat, one pasted prompt, the name and one yes. Simulator, two daemons on one computer, two computers and agents of different people stay separate kinds of evidence. Order of release: the farm service and the site first, then daemons.

Finding 1 (the check on tasks written through the door has no phase): settled by answer 18 as restated. J2 owns the rule: a replay rule and a check before new starts, no allowance, no level change, provenance read at the opening record's anchor, with subtasks and revised rounds defined. Everything written for the earlier reading is gone: the origin check in `level_needed`, the `allow` per door task, the warning 'tasks strangers wrote run here unasked'.

Finding 2 (J1 admitted before the safety check existed): the safety check, the task rule and the first working admission land together in J2, so no build admits a stranger without them. The guards do not depend on the page being on. `only_member` is a closed selector. A role given by the host's explicit command is the one stated exception to 'cannot make anything count'.

Finding 3 (admission by hand skipped checks): one validator for the three paths, rerun at commit time, with the one stated exception that an admission by hand needs no open door. Test `a_rules_change_between_a_request_and_its_admission_is_caught`.

Finding 4 (the admission gate was not the restore guard): the contract's catch-up gate is deleted with its three ways through. Admission reads G1's one contract. A retry of an admission already committed is answered before any gate. The service's answer can only add a hold. A private goal is untouched and never contacts the service.

Finding 5 (the first end was bundled with the backup host): the first door needs E1 and E2, which are built before it; J5 integrates the end and J6 qualifies `door-end` as a gate. Everything about replacing a host and notices to removed computers is left for later. Phases 8 and 9 are plain needs, since the door follows Phase 10. The version ladder is the master plan's.

Finding 6 (page states could not be derived): the host reports one door state and reason, the service stores them and the site prints them; full is its own state and seats used up is a closed reason; the site's overlays are advisory and marked. One test per state: full, seats used, closed by the host, date passed, catching up, off and ended. 'Ended' has one meaning.
Finding 7 (the join plan's confirmation input): the fields the plan id covers are fixed above; advisory facts are left out; one fetch per invocation.

Finding 8 (more inputs than one command): one host command with one plan that includes the rule change; the joiner is asked for the name only; setup is skipped when the agent is connected; J6 counts the journeys.

Finding 9 (avoidable prompts, refusals and warnings), row by row: publish and open are one plan; the default rules are changed inside that plan; one question, for the name; setup skipped when connected and not yet combined with the join; apply-at-once commands run once; no `NameTaken`; `goal join` with a page address works; no conflict from page churn; an admitted retry is answered at once; a deciding role may be given to a door member; a joiner may wait at a full door, with no promise; a listed page may be open; a leave is processed with nobody asked; no 30-day cap; work does not wait on unrelated content; one short disclosure in the host's plan and operational detail in status; the false auto warning is deleted; the permanent 'never restore' warning is replaced by the catching-up state. Kept: the one sharing confirmation, the whole-history disclosure, the required name, the identity and signature checks, the ceilings, conflicts on material changes, and refusal of unsafe rules that have no sound automatic repair.

Finding 10 (names and denial at a door by request): waiting requests are candidates for the shared resolver; a denial is final for that request and no inverse is promised. Tests: deny then ask again; a request that lapsed and asks again; two waiting requests with one name.

Finding 11 (the newcomer blocked by unrelated content, provenance read at the wrong time): no wait on unrelated content, no fetch order, provenance at the authored record's anchor, and the newcomer and readmission cases as tests.

Finding 12 (promises about end, leave and takeover): the end is described as E1 builds it, with what late records still do; the page follows answer 23 and is not taken down by the end; names follow the rule above; nothing is said about a takeover.

Finding 13 (stale recommendations, and qualification of the owner's answers): no decision of the contract is asked again. The acceptance matrix in J6 covers auto on both sides, private invitations after a restart, admission races at the last place, the page turned off with door members present, late content while catching up, and the end with an open door and waiting joiners.

The audit of waits, as the plan states them. Waits on a computer: a join at an open door, a removal after a leave, the recording of plan and file changes, the page (all on the host's computer). Waits on an agent: a door member's task and every result, on a trusted agent. Waits on a person by that person's own choice: a join at a door by request (the host); each task of an agent at level ask (its own person); everything the host's computer signs after a whole-computer restore or a move (the host, one command, answer 13). Removed because they left agents' work waiting on a person by default: the required level, 'wait for my go', the allowance per door task, the gate after every start, the held door, the door closing when the host's agent is disconnected, by request forced on listed pages, removal by hand after a leave, the remove-and-invite path to a role.

Questions for the owner, six and no more, each in everyday words with a recommendation. (1) When you give a role to someone who came through the door, should their agent count as trusted from then on, so that tasks it writes no longer wait and it can approve other strangers' tasks? Recommended: yes. (2) One trusted agent's yes makes a stranger's task available even if another trusted agent, yours included, said no. Recommended: yes; a no that blocks would let one agent stop everything. (3) Someone you let in yourself at a door by request: trusted like a person you invited, or like anyone who came through the door? Recommended: like anyone who came through the door, until you give a role. (4) In a public goal, should the agents of people you invite approve work as your own agent does, without a further command? Recommended: yes; otherwise every result waits for your one agent. (5) Strangers' tasks and results wait while none of the trusted agents is running, because nothing starts an agent by itself yet. Is that acceptable for the first door if your plan and status say so? Recommended: yes, with the release gate that agents approve unprompted. (6) After your Locust data is restored, the door opens again by itself once Locust has caught up or you ran `goal continue`, as the copy last had it; a door you closed after the copy was made would be open again. Recommended: yes, with the door shown in status and in the plan of `goal continue`. The other choice costs one more command after every restore.

phases.title: Callers that are not members
phases.works_afterwards: A daemon's public address holds 64 connections from computers that are not members in about 1 MiB, at most 8 from one source, each with 10 seconds to be admitted. A dial that finds no free slot is deferred and not failed. After an hour of failed exchanges with one computer the daemon tries it once every 15 minutes, which is the only thing that quiets a removed computer in v2. An idle daemon writes at most once a minute. The log of the key that signs members and rules is sent first. `LOCUST_BIND=none` runs through relays only. `doctor --json` reports the counters J6 measures. No signed byte changes.
phases.scope: Holds the contract's J0 nearly whole: the budget and deadline for connections that are not yet admitted, the order in which they are accepted, the deferred dial and the failure backoff, the once-a-minute write of sync state, the governance log first, relay-only running, and the counters. It must not hold any record, any door or admission rule, any change to the 30 second exchange interval, slower dialing for quiet goals (left for later, and the host safety plan's deferred E3 is not built here), or any change to the farm service.
phases.needs: Nothing from the fifteen phases for its behaviour; it can land first, and the simulator needs it above a handful of daemons. It is written on their names: `host` from the roles plan's Phase 1; the governance key's log from K1; and because `lead` is a role name from Phase 4, `Replica::lead_author` becomes `first_author`.

phases.title: The door: public rules, admission and a door member's task
phases.works_afterwards: On two daemons, driven through the operations: a host makes a fresh goal public under rules no stranger can meet and opens a door, to anyone or by request. A stranger's daemon presents the door's description with its chosen name and is admitted with `via: Door`, up to the seats and the ceiling. The door member opens tasks, takes tasks and posts work. Nothing it posts counts without a reviewer, and a task it opens is taken by no agent until a trusted agent approves it. `role give` to a door member works and says what changes. A restarted host admits as before; a host started from an older copy admits nobody until it has caught up. A joiner's daemon stores why it waits and status shows it. Signed bytes change once here.
phases.scope: Holds the publication record that allows joining and the test of when a goal can be made public; `via`; the door record and `door_state`; the five door operations and `goal.join` with a farm reference, on the daemon side of both ends; the one validator with its order; the waiting and denied lists; the five new refusals and the joiner's stored refusal; the `public` preset, the safety check and its callers, reviewers by default in a public goal, and the lines of `role give` and `role take` for a door member; the whole of a door member's task (who is trusted, the approval, the two readings, lists and counts, refusal sentences, board states, what context reads hand out, the pick's evidence, the two skill paragraphs and three operation summaries); the lines the status view gains; row 6 of the signing table with its two tests; and the rule's case in the formal model. It must not hold command lines, plans or their texts (J4); the farm service, the publisher or the page (J3); anything that happens at a leave, an end or a restore beyond reading `Goal::end_held()` and `Node::admission_hold` (J5); a gate of its own on admission; a `held` flag; a refusal for a name already in use; a cap on the closing date; a rule tying listed pages to a door by request; a level check on who wrote a task or an allowance for one; a signed limit on tasks; or any backup-host or takeover rule.
phases.needs: Phase 1: the Host audience, `Node::host()` and `hosts()`, `plan_join` with no grant, every invitation expiring, `invitation.revoke`. Phase 3: levels with auto as the default at a join, `Refused` and `Why`, the trial before signing and `Node::allowed`, the pending lists, `Abilities`. K1: the governance key and `State.host`, `Node::author_alone` and `next_place`, the host's agent that can neither leave nor be removed, `host_may_sign`, admissions signed with no clock reading. Phase 4: `MemberAdmitted.name` and `.role`, `is_member_name`, `RoleHolders` and role lists read at an anchor, `Verifier::latest_review`, `role give` and `role take`, `only_member`, the first-files rule, opinions, the ordered presets, the counting role of `goal add` and `goal invite`. Phase 5: the status view, `render`, 'Waiting for you' and its kinds, `resolve_member` and `member_label`. G1: `Node::admission_hold`, `Refusal::CatchingUp`, `restore_found`. G2: the catching-up words. E1: `Goal::end_held()`. E2: a leaver is removed, so a place frees. Phases 8 and 9: the plan and the files settle by the goal's rule, which the safety check reads. One trial with real agents on the tree as it then stands: do agents act on a listed item that no request record announced.

phases.title: The farm service, the publisher and the page
phases.works_afterwards: The farm service stores a public goal's door beside its snapshot and serves the door's description from one route only. Anyone can publish a page by link; listing still needs the operator. A daemon whose copy is behind the service is told so at its next request and holds. The page shows the Join band with a line for every door state, folds once the visitor copied the prompt or the command or dismissed the band, shows a watch-only view on a phone, and the gallery shows whether a listed goal is open to join or open by request. A page whose host is catching up says joining is paused. The publisher stops retrying a request the service refused for good, and `farm status` says what to run.
phases.scope: Holds what the service stores and answers for a door; the join route; the rule for old requests with the service's number in the answer; link-only publishing without the operator; the quiet and ended retentions and what stays after a delete; the publisher's states, the door in uploads and check-ins, its one report to `Node::guard_attest` (built here as that function's first caller, with G1's two tests), what it may sign above the service's number while its goal is catching up, how it catches up with the service afterwards, and `farm off` on a halted goal; the page's Join band with its states and words, the fold kept in the browser, the phone view, the format-change line of answer 22, names as decided, door members' tasks only once approved, the gallery badge and refresh; nginx limits; generated site types; the site's and the guide's privacy copy. It must not hold the short code, alias routes or the QR code; any admission decision (the service never admits and none of its answers ends a hold); a new command; a second meaning of any door state (it prints J2's `door_state`); or extra roster figures.
phases.needs: J2: the door record, `door_state` with its reasons, the door's description, the approval state of a task in the snapshot. Phase 1: `farm.on` and `farm.off` as the host's operations. K1: the governance key that the page publishes and the host agent's name. Phase 6: the words the site and guides are written in and the test for retired words. G1: `Node::guard_attest` as specified, `Node::admission_hold`. E1: the page reads ended whenever the host's copy holds an end, a suspend carries `ended`, the 30 days start at the first accepted request that says ended, and `farm off` signs nothing for a goal that is ended or catching up.

phases.title: The host's command and the joiner's command
phases.works_afterwards: A host runs `locust --owner farm door open --goal G`, reads one plan and says yes once: the goal has its page, safe rules and an open door, even when it was made with no flags. `farm door close` applies at once; `farm door status`, `farm door admit` and `farm door deny` work. A person pastes the page's prompt into a coding agent or runs `locust --owner farm join ADDRESS`, gives a name, reads one plan and says yes once; their agent joins at auto and starts work without asking. `goal join` with a page address does the same. Status on both sides says where a join stands and what it waits for.
phases.scope: Holds every command line of the door and of joining, with its plan, result and status texts (T1 to T6 rewritten); the fields a join's confirmation is bound to; the sentence of `invitation revoke --all`; the lines a private ticket to a public goal adds to the `goal join` plan; the join prompt that the page copies and its file; the skill's rule for `farm join`; the guide text for the door commands and for joining; and the counted journeys as stated numbers. It must not hold a new daemon operation or record (it calls J2's), a service change, a required `--level` or a question for the level, the words 'wait for my go', a key prefix to pass to the host, required `--seats` or `--expires`, a refusal of `goal join` for a page address, a line about the host agent's level, or any line that asks for a backup host.
phases.needs: J2 and J3. Phase 2: `cli/confirm.rs` with `--plan` and `--confirm`, the inferred `--agent`, `up`, the launcher's block for the owner's commands. Phase 3: the level lines of a join plan and auto as the default. Phase 4: `--name`, `host_name`, `--role` and `--no-role` on `goal add` and `goal invite`. Phase 5: the status view and `render`. Phase 6: the guides and the skill it adds to. G2: the sentence for a host that is catching up. E1: the ended sentence.

phases.title: The life of a public goal
phases.works_afterwards: Every state a public goal passes through reads the same on the host's computer, on a joiner's, at the service and on the page. A newcomer's agent finds no backlog of unread history and starts a ready task without waiting for unrelated content. A door member leaves, is removed with nobody asked, and its place is free. The host ends the goal: the door closes in the same commit, waiting joiners read 'ended by the host', and the page stays 30 days marked ended. After a restore the door is closed with its reason, the page says joining is paused, and one command from the host ends the wait. With the host's computer off the members' work goes on and the page says when it was last seen.
phases.scope: Holds what a newcomer's agent reads first (records from before admission are not unread; the skill section; the newcomer test); leaving and seats on a public goal, on top of E2; removal and what the page and the removed computer show; what `goal end` adds for a public goal (the door cleared in its commit, the plan lines, a plan id that leaves the member list out, the answer to waiting joiners, the page afterwards); a restore and the door (what the host, a joiner and the page see, the door line in the plan of `goal continue` and at `restore_found`, which computers a public host's hold is listed for, scenario tests on several daemons with a door member that never returns); the host's computer off, lost and halted; and the clause `agent revoke` gains. It must not change J2's validator order or any signed field, and must not hold a notice to removed computers, anything about a backup host or a takeover, slower dialing or a slower check-in for quiet goals, a new brief type, a fetch order, or deleting a goal from one's own computer.
phases.needs: J2, J3 and J4. E2: the removal that follows a leave, signed with no clock reading and no new content key. E1: `goal end`, its plan, `revoke_pending`, the ended page. G1 and G2: `Node::hold`, `Node::admission_hold`, `restore_found`, `goal continue` and its plan, the catching-up entry under 'Waiting for you'. K1: `agent revoke` and `agent reconnect`. Phases 3 and 5: the news and pending views a newcomer reads. Phase 6: the skill it adds a section to. J1: the backoff that slows a removed computer.

phases.title: Qualification and release
phases.works_afterwards: The member ceiling is a measured number. A join between two computers on two networks is on record. One page has been watched by 300 streams. Real agents of different owners have joined through the door at 8 and at 16, at auto, with no person answering after the join, and trusted agents approved their tasks unprompted. The restore, end, leave and flood cases pass. The journeys are counted. The farm service and the site are released first, then the daemons, under the number the master plan gives.
phases.scope: Holds the simulator's door scenarios (scale, burst, host offline, flood of connections, waiting at a door by request, a restored host, the end, a leave, a flood of tasks from one door member, the host's record after many joins and leaves); the run on two computers; the viewer test; the runs with real agents and what they record; the release gates and the rule that sets the ceiling; the acceptance matrix of finding 13; the counted journeys; the evidence note and its index entries; the release order and the version numbers. It must not hold new behaviour, and it must not waive a failed authority or approval invariant as a disappointing live run. If the unprompted-approval gate or the task-flood threshold fails, the fallback or the signed limit named in J2 is built before release, in a change of its own.
phases.needs: J1 to J5. Phase 6: the `decide` helper in every harness and `person` in recipes. Phases 7 and 10: their recipes, journey budgets and swarm runs, which this phase adds door cases to and does not repeat. G1: the restore cases it reruns with a door. The master plan's Versions paragraph.

left_for_later: The short code and the QR code on the page, with the alias routes at the service. The first door has one address, the page's.
Extra roster figures in `farm door status`: last sync, events, tasks opened and how many were admitted since the door opened.
A new brief type and a special fetch order for newcomers. A newcomer's agent reads what every member reads.
Telling a removed computer that it was removed. Until then it is refused by every other computer, backs off to one try every 15 minutes, and cannot join again from its stale copy.

Everything about replacing a host: backup-host lines in any plan or page text, a door member as backup host, what a takeover does to a page, a door and its invitations, a new page address after a takeover, and re-keying a page at the service.
Slower dialing and a slower check-in for quiet goals (the host safety plan's deferred E3). Every goal keeps today's 30 seconds.
A signed limit on how many tasks a door member opens. It is built before release only if J6's flood case fails its threshold.
A cutoff on role records, so that taking a role back also binds a changed copy of Locust (the roles plan's Phase 4 leaves it out of v2).
Starting or waking an agent from the daemon, so that a trusted agent approves with no session open.
Letting a trusted agent answer requests at a door by request. In the first door only the host, a person, lets people in.
One plan that covers both setting up Locust on a new computer and the join. The first door shows two plans there.
Limits on what one member can make every other member's computer download.
Deleting a goal from one's own computer, and with it a way for a member to put an ended public goal away.

A door whose open or closed state is signed into the goal, or kept where a restore of the data folder does not reach, which would close the stated limit that a restored copy brings back an older door.

mockups.verdict: Layout still true: the band under the title, the state line, 'Closes Oct 12', 'Hide', one main button 'Copy join prompt' with the command as the quieter choice. Obsolete: the command line `locust --owner join locust.farm/f/KDPQ-MTXB --plan` (it is `locust --owner farm join` with the page's full address and no `--plan`); the QR code, the short address `locust.farm/f/KDPQ-MTXB` and 'Scan to open this page on another device' (left for later); '9 of 16 seats left' (the page shows places free: 'Open · 9 places free'); 'under the public name you choose' (it is 'the name you choose'); the chip 'Participant · Pi' (a named chip or 'Unnamed member'), and coding-agent labels on the chips of members who did not choose to show one. Missing: the line that goals made now end at the next change of signed format (answer 22). 'Needs a Mac with Apple Silicon' was not checked against the build.

Still true: the band folded to one row with the title, the state line and 'Show how to join'. Obsolete wording only: '9 of 16 seats left' becomes '9 places free', and the chip 'Participant · Pi' goes as in the open view.
Still true. Obsolete wording only: '9 of 16 seats left' becomes '9 places free'.

Regenerate. In all four panels that show it, the command line, the QR code and the short address are obsolete as in the open view. Open: seats wording as above. Open by request: 'the host approves each one' becomes 'the host lets each person in', because approve is now what a trusted agent does to a task or a result; '3 waiting' stays. Full: 'all 16 seats taken' and 'Your agent can wait for a seat' are wrong, since a seat is never given back; it reads 'Full · a place opens when someone leaves' and 'Your agent can wait for one.', and the quieter button is right as drawn. Host offline: 'You can start now. The join completes when the host is back.' promises too much; it reads 'The host's computer was last seen 14 min ago. A join started now waits until it is back.' Closed: 'Joining is closed' is still true and now also covers a passed date and used-up seats. Two states are missing: 'Joining is paused · the host's computer is catching up and lets nobody in yet' and 'Ended by the host' with the day the page is removed.

Layout still true: a phone can watch and cannot join, with 'Share' and 'Hide'. Obsolete: the short address `locust.farm/f/KDPQ-MTXB` in large type (there is no short code; the text says to open this page on your Mac and Share sends the full address); '9 of 16 seats left'; 'under the public name you choose'.

Still true in substance, and the contract's instruction to replace the badge is void: under answer 20 a listed farm may be open, so 'Open to join' can stand. Obsolete wording: '9 seats' becomes '9 places free'. A listed farm with a door by request reads 'Open by request'. The label 'Public farm' and the 'Ended' filter stay.

Regenerate. Obsolete: Harbor's roles 'Maintainer, Lead' (the role is 'Reviewer'; there is no maintainer and `public` has no lead); the row 'Participant · Pi' (a named row or 'Unnamed member'); coding-agent labels on rows of members who did not choose to show one. Still true: door members show 'None' under Roles until the host gives one. To add: a mark for the host's agent, the first eight characters of the key beside two members that share a name, and 'Former member' for one who left or was removed. Any caption saying a door member never holds a deciding role is wrong under answer 19.

unsure: What I verified in today's code, at 40221e6: the admission record's two fields (crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:400-403); the review record (event.rs:468-472); the six sync refusals (crates/locust-proto/src/sync.rs:262-278); `plan_join` (crates/locust-core/src/node/peers.rs:302); the service's routes with no join route (crates/locust-farm/src/lib.rs:285-290); the stored receipt returned before the old-sequence test (lib.rs:870-885, 901-903); the enrollment refusal (lib.rs:904-917); `FARM_VERSION` 1, protocol 6 and API 7; the farm commands in crates/locust/src/cli/farm.rs. I did not open fold.rs, chain.rs, views.rs or context.rs; every claim about them is the design's or its attackers', read at 9342514. Everything about behaviour after Phases 3 to 10, K1, G1, G2, E1 and E2 is read from plan text, not from code.

After a restore I let the door follow the restore guard with no flag of its own, as the audit of waits proposes and decision g reads. Row 6 of the signing table, as corrected today, still says a found restore shuts the door until the person opens it again. The fork safety of row 6 does not depend on that flag, but the flag did cover one thing my choice leaves as a stated limit: a restored copy brings back a door the host had closed after the copy was made. G1 revokes pending invitations for the same kind of reason, so a reader may find the two inconsistent. It is owner question 6.

Reviewers by default in a public goal widens Phase 4's counting role, which the corrected roles plan states as covering only a review part the host's agent cannot meet alone ('`public` has no such role'). I chose it so that the agents that make work count are the trusted agents of answer 18 and of the master plan's opening table. The roles plan's author should confirm; without it, every result waits on the host's one agent until the host gives the role. It is owner question 4.

The numbers 64 for default seats and 30 days for the default closing date are mine. Nothing measures them yet. A host could also be given a door with no closing date; I kept a date because a waiting join stops at the description's closing date, and because private invitations always expire.

The command name. I made `farm door open` the one host command and left `farm on` for a read-only page. The contract used `farm on --joinable` followed by `farm door open`. Answer 7 lists publishing among the commands that confirm, and this command does confirm, but the owner has not seen the name.

The publisher signing a check-in that says the door is paused above the service's number while the goal is catching up. The leave design allowed only a delete and a suspend that says ended there. I added the third so that the page can say joining is paused, as decision g requires. It needs the service writer and the host safety plan's author to agree that it is no proof for the guard and does no harm from an old copy.

Whether agents approve door members' tasks from a list with no request record is not shown anywhere. The whole public goal rests on it. I made a trial a need of J2 and a release gate in J6, with an unsigned local fallback; the fallback is not designed in detail.

The pick's evidence. I chose to list the task approval in the pick, as reviews of results are listed. Both attackers say either choice loses something; this one loses the pick for good when the host removes the approver with a cut before the approval. It reaches `directed` and hand-written formations only.

No signed limit on tasks per door member. The first attack suggests one bound that reads only the author's own log. I left it out and made J6's flood case decide. Every computer still stores and folds whatever a door member signs.

When a goal can be made public. I allowed the host's first files and plan text to exist and required only that no task was opened under unsafe rules and no member is on another computer. I did not check how Phase 4's change of rules moves existing shared files into a new epoch, or whether the first files then need sharing again.
`GoalEnded` for every join against an ended goal changes what E1 states for a ticket (`InvitationRefused`). It is a better sentence for the joiner and is terminal too, but E1's text must follow.

A removed computer joining again. The measurement shows that its stale copy answers 'joined' and is not admitted. I state that as a limit. Whether another agent on the same computer can join the same goal was not checked.
